items.headline: Board Marks to Weight Entrance Exams, Says Ministry
items.summary: India's Ministry of Education has announced that it is considering adding board exam marks to the scoring of national entrance examinations. The proposal, discussed in a recent policy review, would give a portion of a student's school board performance weight in the final score for exams such as the Joint Entrance Examination (JEE) and the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET). The move is aimed at reducing the intense pressure on students and creating a more balanced assessment framework. The idea follows years of criticism that the current entrance exam system places disproportionate emphasis on a single test, leading to high stress and limited learning opportunities. Experts argue that incorporating board marks could encourage continuous learning and reduce the 'crash‑course' culture. Similar reforms have been piloted in a few states, with mixed results, and the central government is reviewing data from those experiments. The Ministry has not yet finalized the weightage or the implementation timeline. Officials said a decision will be taken after consultations with state education boards and exam authorities, with a possible announcement by the end of 2024.
